title: What are you using to generate 2D Pixel Art?
author: 0v012
selftext: Hello, I’m working on a 2D game and want to use pixel art. Still struggling with the question where and which AI is best to generate 2D pixel art. Do you have any experience and recommendations?

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: A model will never, to my knowledge, do that on its own. You have to put the output through some processing to get pixel perfect images. Fortunately you can do that through ComfyUI if that's your endgame (hence why the model instructs users to downsize 8x using nearest neighbor). The same goes for indexing colors to adhere to a specific palette, though you'd have to find a node for that, as most true pixel art functions with limited palettes alongside its avoidance of mixels.

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
comments.body:
The best "inspirational" pixel art is, by going, from a normal picture, to a low resolution picture, without using any picture filter (Linear/etc) and go backwards, then use a palette (from Lospec, for example) so you actually maintain the pixel style, so maintain the consistency, and do some dithering if needed (if the palette don't have all the colors you have on the image), if you want to do it with AI, you should first define canvas size and palette, if it can't do any pixel art with those two constraints (and I never have find one that can do that), then that model don't work for what you want  

[Picture](https://imgur.com/GwypnTJ)
This is by app, not by AI

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
So the main issues with using a standard AI tool like Google Nano Banana or Chat GPT image gen for pixel art and sprite sheet animations is that those models dont generate "true" pixel art (their "pixels" are just clumps of smaller pixels with color speckles), can't output transparency, and they have no concept of animation frames. You'll spend more time cleaning up the output than you saved generating it.

https://i.redd.it/sy9vdfnsle5h1.gif

I actually ran into this enough that I ended up building GameLab Studio [https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co) . It generates real pixel art (and other styles too), transparent spritesheets, consistent angles/palette across frames, and tileable textures.
